headline_marked: Jamaat ameer claims [[another revolution is imminent]]
headline: Jamaat ameer claims another revolution is imminent
summary: Shafiqur Rahman calls on citizens to prepare for a new uprising, accusing the government of betraying the people's mandate.
details: Jamaat-e-Islami Ameer and opposition leader Shafiqur Rahman has warned that another revolution is imminent, urging the people of Bangladesh to prepare. He made these remarks during a public rally in Dhaka organized by an 11-party electoral alliance.

Speaking at the south gate of Baitul Mukarram National Mosque, Rahman stated that the struggle against fascism must be uncompromising and intense. He emphasized that the July uprising was a mass movement led by students and youth, not by any single political party.

The Ameer demanded a swift trial for those involved in the July killings and questioned why the people's demands were being ignored. He accused the Prime Minister of betraying the nation by failing to implement the results of the referendum.
Rahman further expressed concern over the return of 'gonoroom-guestroom' culture and fascist behavior in educational institutions, asserting that resistance must be built wherever fascism appears.

Other leaders from the 11-party alliance, including LDP President Colonel (Retd) Oli Ahmed and Bangladesh Khelafat Majlis Ameer Maulana Mamunul Haque, also spoke at the rally, warning the government against creating divisions in society.
caption:

Rahman further expressed concern over the return of 'gonoroom-guestroom' culture and fascist behavior in educational institutions, asserting that resistance must be built wherever fascism appears.

headline_marked: Acting President: [[Supporting July martyrs' families is govt's sacred duty]]
headline: Acting President: Supporting July martyrs' families is govt's sacred duty
summary: Acting President Hafiz Uddin Ahmed says the government must ensure medical treatment for the injured and honor the sacrifices of the July uprising fighters.
details: Acting President Hafiz Uddin Ahmed stated that taking responsibility for the families of those who sacrificed their lives in the student-led uprising and ensuring medical treatment for the injured is the government's most important and sacred duty.

Speaking at a reception for the families of July uprising martyrs and fighters at the Bangladesh-China Friendship Conference Center in Dhaka, he emphasized that the government must help those who lost their sight or limbs during the protests.
He described the July uprising as an opportunity to rebuild the state, aiming for a democratic, just, and corruption-free Bangladesh where every citizen enjoys equal rights and dignity.

The Acting President criticized the ousted Awami League, stating that the current administration will not be like them, and noted that there is no remorse among the party members despite allegations of killings, disappearances, and torture.
He highlighted the importance of democracy and freedom of expression, asserting that as long as these exist, the country's independence and sovereignty will remain intact.
During the event, a video documentary was shown that omitted the images of martyr Abu Sayeed and BNP Chairperson Begum Khaleda Zia, leading to protests from the attendees.
Hafiz Uddin Ahmed expressed deep regret and mistakes can be made, but he was pained that this occurred in front of foreign guests, which he suggested would please those in the 'neighboring country'.
He reiterated that Abu Sayeed is the symbol of the July revolution and any documentary on the movement should be complete only with his image.
caption:
Supporting the families of July martyrs is a 'sacred duty' for the government, says Acting President Hafiz Uddin Ahmed.

Acting President Hafiz Uddin Ahmed stated that taking responsibility for the families of those who sacrificed their lives in the student-led uprising and ensuring medical treatment for the injured is the government's most important and sacred duty.

Speaking at a reception for the families of July uprising martyrs and fighters at the Bangladesh-China Friendship Conference Center in Dhaka, he emphasized that the government must help those who lost their sight or limbs during the protests.

He described the July uprising as an opportunity to rebuild the state, aiming for a democratic, just, and corruption-free Bangladesh where every citizen enjoys equal rights and dignity.

The Acting President criticized the ousted Awami League, stating that the current administration will not be like them, and noted that there is no remorse among the party members despite allegations of killings, disappearances, and torture.

He highlighted the importance of democracy and freedom of expression, asserting that as long as these exist, the country's independence and sovereignty will remain intact.

During the event, a video documentary was shown that omitted the images of martyr Abu Sayeed and BNP Chairperson Begum Khaleda Zia, leading to protests from the attendees.

Hafiz Uddin Ahmed expressed deep regret and mistakes can be made, but he was pained that this occurred in front of foreign guests, which he suggested would please those in the 'neighboring country'.

He reiterated that Abu Sayeed is the symbol of the July revolution and any documentary on the movement should be complete only with his image.
